questions.prompt: Put the signs in place of each * in order so that the equation is true. Which set of signs is right?
questions.rule: Try each set of signs in turn. Do × and ÷ first (left to right), then + and −.

questions.prompt: K means +, L means ×, N means − and M means ÷. Which letters, put in place of each * in order, make the equation true?
questions.rule: Write the equation again with the real signs, then work it out: × and ÷ first, then + and −.

questions.prompt: Here + means ÷, × means +, − means × and ÷ means −. Which equation is correct?
questions.rule: Write each option again with the real signs (+ → ÷, × → +, − → ×, ÷ → −), then work it out: × and ÷ first, then + and −.

questions.prompt: Here + means ÷, × means +, − means × and ÷ means −. Which equation is correct?
questions.rule: Write each option again with the real signs (+ → ÷, × → +, − → ×, ÷ → −), then work it out: × and ÷ first, then + and −.
questions.working: (p + q) − q × p → (p ÷ q) × q + p = p + p = 2p

questions.prompt: Which two signs must be swapped to make the equation true?
questions.rule: Swap the two signs everywhere they appear, then work out the left side: × and ÷ first, then + and −.

questions.prompt: Which two numbers must be swapped to make the equation true?
questions.rule: Swap the two numbers, then work out the left side: × and ÷ first, then + and −.
questions.note: As printed, the equation is already true (5 + 3 − 3 = 5). Of the four swaps, only 3 and 2 keeps it true.
